applyTo: "**/*.md"

# Documentation style instructions

- Keep content concise, specific, and task-oriented.
- Prefer direct user-facing language over boilerplate or marketing language.
- Use complete Adobe product names on first mention in external documentation.
- Use [!DNL Adobe Experience Platform] and [!DNL Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition] in external-facing content where product names are mentioned.
- Replace acronym-only references such as "AEP" and "AJO B2B" with the full product name in user-facing text.
- Do not use "below" or "above" to describe document structure; use "following," "previous," or "in the next section" instead.
- Avoid generic sections such as "Related topics" or "FAQ" unless the content pattern requires them.
- Do not add a references list or "Related topics" section at the end of an article. Place links where they are relevant in the content, and explain how each destination relates to the current topic.
- Preserve exact technical names and dataset IDs when they are required by the source contract.
